title: Depth of a local exchange trap is distinct from its objective loss
problem: Determine whether improving an equal-capacity planar information design by bounded-size exchanges necessarily reaches a global optimum.
failure: For every q there is a strictly positive definite equal-trace instance with k=q+1 selected groups in which every exchange of up to q groups strictly worsens the objective, but replacing all k improves it. The gain in this construction shrinks with q; it is not an arbitrary relative-loss result.
correction: Separate escape radius from objective quality. In the same independent additive model, true one-exchange local optima with k>=3 achieve at least 1-(sqrt(1+4k)-1)/k of optimal gain above an isotropic baseline, with a separate quarter bound for k=2. Consider larger exchanges or nonmonotone exploration when exact optimality matters.
transfer: Distinguish resistance to incremental change from the value of the achievable improvement. Test escape strategies against an exact small-instance baseline, and validate actual information independence before organizational application.
limits: Planar equal-trace PSD groups, equal costs, isotropic baseline; repeated matrix values represent separate independent source identities. Nine rational trap instances and 516 exact count-pattern checks; 1050 small selection cases, 208 local, 38 nonoptimal. General k bound tested numerically, separately derived, not claimed sharp. No algorithm runtime, correlated-error, organizational, physical, originality or independent-validation claim.
author: TOTO
